editorial.headline: Company Training for the Fields, Farms and Fisheries
editorial.standfirst: A company-run training activity spanning agricultural, livestock and fisheries skills, nationally open to full foreign ownership and not blocked by Bali’s moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is for company-organised job training that builds practical capability across the agricultural and fisheries economy. Its remit is unusually broad: agricultural mechanisation, food crops, horticulture, mixed farming, soil cultivation and land conservation sit alongside crop cultivation, fishing, fish farming, fisheries machinery, and the processing of agricultural, fisheries and livestock products. It also reaches into production agribusiness for crops, livestock and aquatic resources. The common thread is not the particular technique being taught, but training arranged by a company to deepen work skills and expertise.

That organising role matters. The classification describes training conducted by a company, giving it a distinctly operational character: it is about developing capability in the industries named, rather than merely presenting agricultural or fisheries subjects in the abstract. The record does not name particular business scales open to the activity, so no scale distinction should be inferred from it. What is clear is the breadth of the technical and production knowledge that can fall within a company’s training programme.

Foreign investment is permitted nationally for this activity, with ownership allowed up to 100%. That is the national position stated for the activity, and it should be kept separate from Bali’s local investment treatment. In Bali, this activity is not blocked by the province-wide moratorium that applies to all low- and medium-low-risk activities for PMA. Its Bali status is marked as medium-high/high risk, with verification required for the specific address.

The practical reading is therefore straightforward but not casual: a foreign-owned company may pursue this activity nationally with up to full foreign ownership, while Bali does not impose the moratorium block recorded for lower-risk activities. The local position is still address-sensitive, so the classification supports neither complacency nor a broader claim than the record permits. It identifies a company training activity with national foreign-investment openness and a Bali pathway that remains available subject to address verification.
